FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Cymoxanil, technical is employed in the preparation of fungicidal formulations for agricultural use. Cymoxanil is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization ~-cyano-N-[ ( ethylamino ) carbonyl ]-2-( methoxyimino ) acetamide. The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of cymoxanil are given below.
Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass

( 1S0 ) for

C7H10N403

N=C-C-C-NH-C-NH-CHZCH3 II NOCH3 In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides A c(, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 1S 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same.as that of the specified value in this standard.

DETERMINATION OF CYMOXANIL CONTENT A-1 PRINCIPLE Cymoxanil content is determined by high performance liquid chromatography ( HPLC ) using internal standard technique. .A-2 APPARATUS A-2.1 High Performance Liquid Chramatograph, equipped with a constant flow pump, -constant temperature column compartment, sample injector capabje of injecting 25 pl aliquots, a 254 m wavelength ultraviolet detector.artd a recorder ( digital integrator or other data handjing device ) is used for this determination. The suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided standardization is done: Column Reverse phase C8, C 18 or equivalent pre-packed column, 4.6x 250mm Ambient Acetonitrile : Water ( 2"5 :75, v/v ), pH of water= 2.8 adjusted with 85 percent phosphoric acid ( H~pOq) 1.5ml/min A-2.5 Ultrasonic Bath A-2.+ Standard Glassware A-3 REAGENTS A-3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC grade. A-3.2 HPLC Grade Water A-3.3 Acetanilide, (
purity. internal standard ] of known

A-3.4 Cymoxanil, purity. A-3.5 Ortho 85 percent.

analytical standard of known Acid, HPLC grade,

Phosphoric

A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase Adjust the pH of water to 2.8 with ortho phosphoric acid. Add 1 500 ml of the pH 2.8 adjusted water to 500 ml of acetonitrile in a flask , mix thoroughly. Filter the mixture using the fikering apparatus. A-4.2 Preparation of Internal Standard Weigh accurately 400 mg of acetanilide into a 100ml volumetric flask. Makeup to volume with HPLC grade acetonitrile and ultrasonicate for 5 min. A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution Weigh accurately 35 mg of cymoxanil analytical standard of known purity and add it into a 25 ml volumetric flask. Pipette 5 ml ofacetanilide internal standard solution into the volumetric flask. Make up to volume with acetonitrile and mix. Dissolve ultrasonically for 5 min and filter the standard solution through 0.45 pm filter. 2

IS 15600:2005 A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution Weigh accurately 35 mg of cymoxanil,-technical and add it into a 25-ml volumetric flask. Pipette 5 ml of internal standard solution in the flask. Make up to volume with acetonitrile, mix and ultrasonicate for 5 min. Filter the solution through the 0.45 pm filter. A-4.5 Estimation A-4.5.1 Equilibrate the column with the mobile phase for 45 min before injecting the standard/sample. After the column has equilibrated and a stable baseline is obtained, inject. in duplicate, 20 p] each of standard and sample solution. A-4.5.2 Retention Time Cymoxanil : 13.Omin 8.4 min 15.Omin given in the Calculation ( see A-5). .Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also rewiewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed whensuch review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for~evision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
